question.problem: The solution to the inequality $-5y+16\le -4$ is $y${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $16$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5y+16 & \le -4 \\ -5y+16-16 & \le -4-16 \\ -5y+0 & \le -20 \\ -5y & \le -20\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-5.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5y\,\, & \le \,\,-20 \\ \frac{-5y}{-5}\, & \ge \,\,\frac{-20}{-5} \\ \frac{\cancel{-5}y}{\cancel{-5}}\, & \ge \,\,4 \\ y\,\, & \ge \,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y\ge 4.$
